claims.author: ajtowns
claims.harm: LogInfo called during global initialization prior to InitLogger() could fail or misbehave with a shared dispatcher
claims.quote: This seems like a regression. With this approach you can't assume LogInfo called during global initialization won't be called prior to InitLogger()

settled_by.quote: I've changed the approach to your suggestion, so marking this as resolved.

claims.author: ajtowns
claims.harm: Unnecessary performance overhead in log-checking paths caused by std::function indirection
claims.quote: Jumping through a std::function when we could just be checking an atomic bitfield doesn't seem like a good approach.

settled_by.quote: The indirection is gone, and this PR now doesn't touch util/node logging (including logging statement evaluation) at all

claims.author: purpleKarrot
claims.harm: Unnecessary complexity from supporting multi-connection callbacks and userdata when the logger is internally global
claims.quote: I doubt that there is an actual use case for multiple logging connections. The logger is global internally and can be handled as global by clients as well

settled_by.quote: I think this concern is orthogonal to the changes proposed in this PR, so I think that conversation might be better had e.g. in #30342 ?

claims.author: purpleKarrot
claims.harm: Using singletons introduces viral coupling across kernel components
claims.quote: Now everybody should understand why singletons are *viral* and therefore should be forbidden. I have zero tolerance for such code.

claims.author: ajtowns
claims.harm: Breaks code that relies on side-effects inside logging arguments if LogInfo argument evaluation is made conditional
claims.quote: I think your latest implementation (a4e8f3c8d6763a95c1804fc40781b379e6127b66) is dangerously wrong, btw -- LogInfo() etc currently always evaluate their arguments

settled_by.quote: The easiest way to ensure any potential/accidental side-effects don't make the behaviour brittle is to always evaluate the logging statements, which is what our code currently does

claims.author: w0xlt
claims.harm: Memory leak of user_data and connection allocation if std::bad_alloc is thrown during callback registration
claims.quote: RegisterCallback() and LogDebug() can also throw std::bad_alloc. btck_LoggingConnection can be a smart pointer.

settled_by.quote: Fixed by wrapping user data in a RAII UserData wrapper, and the callback in a RAII CallbackHandle wrapper.

claims.author: w0xlt
claims.harm: Deadlock if std::bad_alloc during list insertion destroys temporary callback while holding the logger mutex and user_data destruction interacts with the logger
claims.quote: If that callback destroys another logging connection, it tries to acquire the same mutex and deadlocks, preventing btck_logging_connection_create from returning nullptr.

settled_by.quote: Force-pushed to address a (hard to reach) deadlock issue flagged by @w0xlt

notes: Objections from ajtowns (std::function overhead, side effects, init ordering) and w0xlt (bad_alloc leaks and callback mutex deadlock) were resolved with pushed fixes. purpleKarrot's objection against singletons remains open as the author asked for alternatives without follow-up.

participants.note: Concept and approach ACK; provided rebase branches, suggested separating move-only commits and removing indirection overhead
Raised concerns regarding std::function overhead, global initialization order regressions, and conditional evaluation of LogInfo arguments
Objected to singleton pattern usage in the logger and questioned the multi-connection logging interface
Found potential resource leaks and a mutex deadlock risk if bad_alloc occurs during callback registration

support.author: ryanofsky
support.reason: Major concept and approach ACK. This seems thoughtfully implemented to be minimally disruptive to existing code while rationalizing the kernel logging API
